messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: capacity surge detected in us-west-2 inference pool (sev3) — elevated token throttles and rising 5xxs. Alert: capacity_surge_v2. See <https://internal.monitoring/redwood/alerts/1234|alert>
anna (SRE, oncall): I'm on it. Initial triage: seeing tokens/sec spike and queue depth climbing on pool-gpu-13. Customers reporting slow responses and some 502s. Paging devin and liam. @sophia can you collect a short customer impact summary?
devin (Eng-SRE): Got it. I can increase burst capacity for that pool right now. Before I do, what's current queue depth and tokens/sec? Sending queries.
liam (Runtime): FYI kernel hot-path metrics show KV-cache eviction spikes at the same time. Could be workload with large prefixes. I'm pulling more traces.
sophia (Support): Two paying customers hit significant latency (SLO breaches). Customer A (enterprise) sees 30% error rate on inference endpoint, Customer B (SaaS) has 15% error rate. Notified both, they want ETA.
anna (SRE, oncall): ETA: temporary mitigation within 10m, will update customers once mitigated.
devin (Eng-SRE): Running quick scale bump: `infra scale-pool --pool us-west-2/gpu-pool-1 --delta 4 --reason "emergency burst"` — executing now. Also enabling fallback routing to dedicated-2 for non-sensitive models.
liam (Runtime): Command accepted. While that spins up, I suggest applying two short-term mitigations: 1) reduce batching window for low-priority routes; 2) disable background quantization jobs. Quick commands:
```
# reduce batcher window
runtimectl set-config --pool gpu-pool-1 --batch-window-ms 12
# pause non-essential jobs
jobctl pause --tag background-quant
```
anna (SRE, oncall): Doing both. Batch window change applied. Background jobs paused.
devin (Eng-SRE): New nodes are coming up. Checking queue depth histogram:
```
max(queue_depth) = 6800
p95(queue_depth) = 4200
tokens/sec (pool) = 1.9M
throttle_events/5m = 312
```
liam (Runtime): That max is concerning. We should avoid immediate permanent alert changes, but we need to tune noise post-stabilization.
anna (SRE, oncall): Customers updated: Sophia please send the line that we plan 30m mitigation window and to expect some degraded latency for the next 20–30 minutes.
sophia (Support): Sent. Customers acknowledged. They said to keep them posted.
devin (Eng-SRE): Traffic shifted ~18% to dedicated-2. Error rate dropping to ~6% now.
anna (SRE, oncall): Good. Monitor for 15m. If stable, remove emergency scale after 60m and then follow up with a post-incident plan.
liam (Runtime): Quick note from traces: big tail requests often originate from a small set of models with long context (>= 8k tokens) and low cache hit. Suggest adding model-level rate-limits for those until we have a proper fix.
devin (Eng-SRE): I can add a short-term rate-limit rule: `route: model-long-context-* -> max_tokens_per_minute: 10000` — rolling now.
anna (SRE, oncall): Nice. Also flagging the alert noise vector: capacity_surge_v2 fires frequently when short spikes occur — it currently alerts on a 1m average. That caused a bunch of pings during today's noisy periods.
liam (Runtime): Agreed. Proposal for post-incident tuning (quick bullets):
- Require sustained condition: change alert to `sustained 5m` (from 1m)
- Use `p95(queue_depth) > 3500` instead of instantaneous max
- Add `tokens/sec per-GPU > 300k for 5m` as a secondary signal
- Add a throttle spike alert: `increase in throttle_events rate > 200% over baseline (5m)`
- Add dashboard panels: per-pool `queue_depth histogram`, `tokens/sec per-GPU`, `model-level long-context traffic`, `KV-cache hit rate`

anna (SRE, oncall): I like that. Let's make concrete alert rule diffs in a PR. Devin, can you own the alert changes? Devin -> liam for dashboard wiring and runbook updates. I'll own the customer-facing timeline & post-incident writeup.
devin (Eng-SRE): I can do the alert PR now, will include tests. Suggested new PromQL for main alert:
```
# trigger when p95 queue depth sustained > 3500 for 5m
qdp95 = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(pool_queue_depth_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))
alert: PoolQueueDepthHigh
expr: qdp95{pool="us-west-2/gpu-pool-1"} > 3500
for: 5m
```
liam (Runtime): I'll add panels to grafana and wire in model-level time series. Also add an explainer widget showing which models contribute to p95.
anna (SRE, oncall): Action items summary (quick):
- devin: alert PR + unit tests (due EOD)
- liam: dashboards + runbook snippets for decision tree (due tomorrow)
- anna: incident summary + customer timeline (due today)
- sophia: follow-up customer comms and escalations (ongoing)
- ops: evaluate permanent capacity bump for us-west-2 (ops leads)

sophia (Support): Customers asked for a postmortem once the writeup is ready. I'll keep them in the loop.
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: status -> mitigated. Notes: error rate dropping, burst scale executed, traffic partially rerouted.
anna (SRE, oncall): Marking incident as mitigated for now. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. Please log any oddities here.
devin (Eng-SRE): Filing PR: <https://git.internal/redwood/alerts/pulls/789> — includes change to `for: 5m`, switching to p95, and adding `tokens_per_gpu` rule. Tests included.
liam (Runtime): Dashboard PR: <https://git.internal/redwood/grafana/pulls/112> — added panels, and a template var for `model_prefix` to debug long-context.
anna (SRE, oncall): Post-incident follow-ups I want discussed in our blameless review:
- Why did KV-cache hit rate drop simultaneously? (liam)
- Should we adopt soft limits for long-context models? (product + runtime)
- Can we make emergency burst scaling automated with guardrails (cost window)? (infra)
- How to reduce alert noise for transient spikes across regions (alerting)

liam (Runtime): I'll prepare a short experiment to increase KV-cache size for affected pools and measure impact. If results are good, propose a config knob for dynamic cache scaling.
devin (Eng-SRE): Also adding a short checklist to the runbook: on a capacity surge -> (1) reduce batch window (2) pause background jobs (3) temporary routing to dedicated pools (4) short-term model rate-limits -> then re-evaluate after 30m.
anna (SRE, oncall): Thanks all. Closing thread for real once postmortem doc is linked. Current status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next meeting: blameless review tomorrow 10:30am PT.
